issues.legal_issue: A pending application for relief under a provision that is omitted by a retrospectively applicable amendment cannot be decided under that omitted provision.
material_facts: A decree for possession had been made against a tenant, and execution proceedings were pending when the original protective legislation came into force.
While execution remained pending, the tenant applied for the decree to be rescinded or varied under a provision empowering courts to grant that relief.
The application remained undecided when an amendment omitted that provision and applied the amended legislation to proceedings pending at an earlier commencement point.
The application was still pending when the amendment became effective.
issues.conclusion: The application had to be dismissed because the retrospectively applicable amended legislation had removed the court’s power to grant relief under the omitted provision.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 8 of the Bengal General Clauses Act, repeal ordinarily does not affect accrued rights or pending proceedings unless a contrary intention appears. Provisions creating or taking away substantive rights are ordinarily prospective, but may operate retrospectively by express words or necessary implication, and only to that extent. Legislative intention is gathered from the words’ plain, normal, grammatical meaning. Ambiguity in beneficent legislation should be resolved to preserve the benefit, and a grammatical reading producing absurdity or inconsistency may be rejected; neither principle applies where the language is unambiguous. Section 1(2) of the Calcutta Thika Tenancy Amendment Act, 1953 applied the amended Act to pending proceedings, and “amended” covered omissions as well as additions and alterations. Because section 28 of the 1949 Act was omitted, the court no longer had power to grant relief in applications still pending. The contrary view in Deorajan Debi v. Satyadhan Ghosal, (1953) 58 C.W.N. 64, was overruled.

predicates.pending_execution_case: A proceeding to execute a possession decree against a tenant was pending.
predicates.relief_application_pending_when_amendmen: The tenant’s application for relief against the decree remained undecided when the amendment took effect.
predicates.amended_framework_applied_retroactively_: The legislature made the amended framework apply retrospectively to proceedings that were pending at an earlier point.
predicates.relief_granting_power_removed: The amendment removed the power that had enabled courts to grant the requested relief.

issues.definition: When an execution proceeding and the tenant’s relief application remain pending as a retrospectively applicable amendment removes the court’s power to grant that relief, the application is dismissed.

issues.legal_issue: A High Court bench that cannot distinguish an earlier decision of a bench of coordinate jurisdiction and considers it wrong must refer the issue to a larger bench rather than overrule the earlier decision.
material_facts: An earlier decision of a coordinate bench of the High Court addressed the same legal issue.
The later bench could not distinguish the earlier decision and considered its view wrong.
The later bench rejected the earlier decision without referring the issue to a larger bench.
issues.conclusion: The later bench should have referred the matter to a larger bench instead of overruling the coordinate bench’s decision.
issues.legal_principle: Judicial decorum and legal propriety require certainty in the law. A High Court bench cannot overrule an indistinguishable decision of a coordinate bench merely because it considers that decision wrong; it must refer the issue to a larger bench. The same principle applies when a single judge disagrees with an earlier single-judge decision. The Court noted the uniform practice of the High Courts and the Calcutta High Court rule dating from 1867.

predicates.high_court_case: A legal issue is before a High Court bench or a single High Court judge.
predicates.indistinguishable_coordinate_bench_decis: An earlier decision by a bench of coordinate jurisdiction addresses the issue and cannot be distinguished.
predicates.later_bench_considers_earlier_decision_w: The later bench considers the earlier decision legally wrong.

issues.definition: When a High Court case presents an indistinguishable decision of coordinate jurisdiction that the later bench considers wrong, the issue is referred to a larger bench.
